title: Scotland
description: Bank holidays in Scotland, with Easter Sunday

festivals.name: New Year’s Day
festivals.meaning: A bank holiday in Scotland since 1871. When it falls at a weekend, a weekday is given in its place.

festivals.name: 2 January bank holiday
festivals.gloss: the second day of the year
festivals.meaning: A Scottish bank holiday since 1973, giving two days for the New Year. When it falls at a weekend, a weekday is given in its place.

festivals.name: Good Friday
festivals.meaning: Marks the crucifixion. A bank holiday in Scotland since 1871.

festivals.name: Easter Sunday
festivals.meaning: The Christian feast of the resurrection, on the Sunday after the church’s full moon on or after 21 March, so between 22 March and 25 April. It isn’t a bank holiday, being a Sunday.

festivals.name: Early May bank holiday
festivals.meaning: A Scottish bank holiday since 1871. England, Wales and Northern Ireland only got theirs in 1978. It moved to Monday 8 May in 1995 for the 50th anniversary of VE Day, and to Friday 8 May in 2020 for the 75th.

festivals.name: Spring bank holiday
festivals.meaning: The last Monday in May, a Scottish bank holiday since 1978. It moved into June for Elizabeth II’s Golden, Diamond and Platinum Jubilees.

festivals.name: Summer bank holiday
festivals.meaning: One of the first bank holidays, set by the Bank Holidays Act 1871. Scotland kept it on the first Monday when England and Wales moved theirs to the last.

festivals.name: St Andrew’s Day
festivals.meaning: Scotland’s national day, a bank holiday since the St Andrew’s Day Bank Holiday (Scotland) Act 2007. When it falls at a weekend, the next Monday is the holiday.

festivals.name: Christmas Day
festivals.meaning: A bank holiday in Scotland since 1871. When it falls at a weekend, a weekday is given in its place.

festivals.name: Boxing Day
festivals.meaning: A bank holiday in Scotland since 1973. When it falls at a weekend, a weekday is given in its place.

festivals.name: Royal wedding bank holiday
festivals.meaning: An extra bank holiday for the wedding of Princess Anne and Mark Phillips.

festivals.name: Silver Jubilee bank holiday
festivals.meaning: An extra bank holiday for the Queen’s Silver Jubilee. England, Wales and Northern Ireland had theirs a day later.

festivals.name: Royal wedding bank holiday
festivals.meaning: An extra bank holiday for the wedding of Prince Charles and Lady Diana Spencer.

festivals.name: Millennium bank holiday
festivals.meaning: An extra bank holiday to mark the new millennium.

festivals.name: Golden Jubilee bank holiday
festivals.meaning: An extra bank holiday for the Queen’s Golden Jubilee, next to the moved spring bank holiday.

festivals.name: Royal wedding bank holiday
festivals.meaning: An extra bank holiday for the wedding of Prince William and Catherine Middleton.

festivals.name: Diamond Jubilee bank holiday
festivals.meaning: An extra bank holiday for the Queen’s Diamond Jubilee, next to the moved spring bank holiday.

festivals.name: Platinum Jubilee bank holiday
festivals.meaning: An extra bank holiday for the Queen’s Platinum Jubilee, next to the moved spring bank holiday.

festivals.name: State Funeral of Queen Elizabeth II
festivals.meaning: A one-off bank holiday for the Queen’s state funeral.

festivals.name: Coronation of King Charles III
festivals.meaning: A one-off bank holiday for the coronation, two days after it.

festivals.name: World Cup bank holiday
festivals.meaning: A one-off bank holiday in Scotland during the 2026 men’s football World Cup, which Scotland qualified for.
